req.title: Task creation persists
req.statement: The system shall commit new task rows so subsequent GET calls return them across requests.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /tasks/ must commit new task rows so subsequent GET calls return them. I design: (1) a positive EP test that creates a valid task and verifies the 201 response payload plus persistence via GET /tasks/{id}; (2) a negative NEG test that sends a missing required field and expects 422; (3) a BVA test at the title length boundary (exactly 100 chars, then 101 chars) to catch off-by-one mutations on the max_length constraint; (4) a STC test verifying the full state transition: task absent → created → retrievable via list endpoint with correct count delta; (5) a DT test covering the completed=True branch to catch boolean-negation mutations on the default=False field. All tests use in-process TestClient, assert exact status codes and field values, and account for the 20 pre-loaded rows.

tests.name: test_create_task_positive_persists_via_get
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: POST /tasks/ with valid title, description, completed=false
Assert 201 response with correct payload fields
GET /tasks/{id} using id from create response
Assert GET returns 200 and identical payload
expected: Response body contains title, description, completed=false, id=21
GET /tasks/21 returns HTTP 200 with same title and completed=false
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_create_task_positive_persists_via_get():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Integration test task", "description": "Verify persistence", "completed": False}
    r_post = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    body = r_post.json()
    assert body["title"] == "Integration test task"
    assert body["description"] == "Verify persistence"
    assert body["completed"] == False
    assert "id" in body
    assert "created_at" in body
    task_id = body["id"]
    r_get = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    get_body = r_get.json()
    assert get_body["id"] == task_id
    assert get_body["title"] == "Integration test task"
    assert get_body["description"] == "Verify persistence"
    assert get_body["completed"] == False

test_create_task_positive_persists_via_get()

tests.name: test_create_task_title_boundary_100_and_101_chars
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: POST /tasks/ with title of exactly 100 characters — expect 201
POST /tasks/ with title of exactly 101 characters — expect 422
expected: 100-char title: HTTP 201, title in response equals the 100-char string
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_create_task_title_boundary_100_and_101_chars():
    client = TestClient(app)
    title_100 = "A" * 100
    r_ok = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": title_100, "completed": False})
    assert r_ok.status_code == 201
    body_ok = r_ok.json()
    assert body_ok["title"] == title_100
    assert len(body_ok["title"]) == 100
    title_101 = "A" * 101
    r_bad = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": title_101, "completed": False})
    assert r_bad.status_code == 422
    r_list = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r_list.status_code == 200
    tasks = r_list.json()
    assert len(tasks) == 21

test_create_task_title_boundary_100_and_101_chars()

tests.name: test_create_task_state_transition_absent_to_retrievable_in_list
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: GET /tasks/ to capture baseline count (must be 20)
GET /tasks/ again and assert count increased by exactly 1
Assert the new task appears in the list with correct id and title
expected: After POST, GET returns exactly 21 tasks
New task found in list by id with matching title
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_create_task_state_transition_absent_to_retrievable_in_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r_before = client.get("/tasks/", params={"limit": 1000})
    assert r_before.status_code == 200
    before = r_before.json()
    assert len(before) == 20
    payload = {"title": "State transition task", "completed": False}
    r_post = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    new_id = r_post.json()["id"]
    r_after = client.get("/tasks/", params={"limit": 1000})
    assert r_after.status_code == 200
    after = r_after.json()
    assert len(after) == len(before) + 1
    assert len(after) == 21
    ids_in_list = [t["id"] for t in after]
    assert new_id in ids_in_list
    matched = next(t for t in after if t["id"] == new_id)
    assert matched["title"] == "State transition task"
    assert matched["completed"] == False

test_create_task_state_transition_absent_to_retrievable_in_list()

tests.name: test_create_task_completed_true_persists_correctly
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: GET /tasks/?completed=true and assert new task appears in filtered list
expected: Filtered GET with completed=true includes the new task
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_create_task_completed_true_persists_correctly():
    client = TestClient(app)
    payload = {"title": "Already done task", "description": "Completed on creation", "completed": True}
    r_post = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r_post.status_code == 201
    body = r_post.json()
    assert body["completed"] == True
    assert body["title"] == "Already done task"
    task_id = body["id"]
    r_get = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    assert r_get.json()["completed"] == True
    r_filtered = client.get("/tasks/", params={"completed": "true", "limit": 1000})
    assert r_filtered.status_code == 200
    filtered = r_filtered.json()
    filtered_ids = [t["id"] for t in filtered]
    assert task_id in filtered_ids
    for t in filtered:
        assert t["completed"] == True

test_create_task_completed_true_persists_correctly()
